hook: Before modern sewage treatment, many rivers below cities had stretches where almost nothing could live: the water smelled, fish were gone, and swimmers got sick. Today a city of a million people can return its wastewater to a river clean enough for fish. The trick is a series of steps that copy what nature does, only faster and in a small space.

prereq.q: In the eutrophication chain, what uses up dissolved oxygen?
options: Decomposers breaking down dead organic matter
prereq.why: Decomposers respire as they break down organic matter, using oxygen.

prereq.q: Which is a point source of water pollution?
options: Exhaust from all cars in a city
prereq.why: An outfall is a single pipe, a point source.

figure.caption: Primary treatment is physical, secondary is biological, tertiary removes nutrients, and disinfection kills germs before release.

chain.cause: Screens and settling tanks remove debris and let solids sink (primary)
chain.effect: large objects, grit and much of the solid matter are removed as sludge

chain.cause: Microbes in aerated tanks eat the dissolved organic matter (secondary)
chain.effect: BOD falls, so the waste will not use up the river's oxygen

chain.cause: Filters and chemicals remove nitrogen and phosphorus (tertiary)
chain.effect: nutrients that would feed algal blooms are kept out of the river

chain.cause: Chlorine, ozone or UV light treats the water (disinfection)
chain.effect: germs are killed before the water is released

chain.cause: Sludge is digested, dried and disposed of or reused
chain.effect: methane can be captured for energy and solids are landfilled, burned or spread as fertilizer

ideas: Primary treatment: physical. Screens, grit chambers and settling tanks remove solids as sludge.
Secondary treatment: biological. Microbes in aerated tanks break down dissolved organic matter, cutting BOD so the river keeps its oxygen.
Tertiary treatment: removes nitrogen and phosphorus (preventing eutrophication) and other chemicals. Then disinfection with chlorine, ozone or UV kills germs.
Homes without sewers use a septic system: a tank where solids settle and a drain field where soil filters the liquid. Combined sewers can overflow untreated sewage in heavy rain.

misconception.wrong: Sewage treatment just filters the water.
misconception.right: Filtering and settling are only the first step. Secondary treatment uses living microbes to eat the dissolved waste, and tertiary treatment and disinfection remove nutrients and kill germs.

summary: Sewage treatment cleans wastewater in stages. Primary treatment physically removes solids as sludge; secondary treatment uses microbes in aerated tanks to break down dissolved organic matter and cut BOD; tertiary treatment removes nitrogen and phosphorus; disinfection kills germs. Sludge is digested and disposed of or reused. Septic systems treat wastewater for single homes, and combined sewers can overflow in storms.
